paths.title: Software Engineering Core to ML Route
paths.why_it_fits:
Aligns with your current JEE
preparation and strong PCM background. A foundational computer science degree
builds the precise software architecture, backend, and system design skills that
distinguish an AI/ML Engineer from a pure Data Scientist. You can prioritize
institutions that align with your stated budget constraint while securing strong
technical fundamentals.
tradeoffs:
First-year engineering curricula
mandate general science and hardware courses, which temporarily diverts time
away from focused software or ML learning.

Traditional degrees often teach
advanced ML only as late-stage electives, requiring you to self-direct your
ML-specific project building in earlier years.

milestones.focus:
Protect exam study time while maintaining a coding habit within
the 5-10 hours/week limit

Strengthen
foundational programming and version control as time frees up

Core Problem Solving and Backend
Fundamentals
projects: Basic Web Scraper for Automated Data Collection

milestones.focus: Applied ML Foundations and API Development
projects: Basic REST API to serve a machine learning prediction

Automated Data Pipeline deployed in a Docker
container

internship_strategy.readiness:
Demonstrated ability to
write clean, version-controlled code, implement basic data structures, and build
functional backend logic integrating a database.
preparation:
Maintain clean, well-documented project repositories on
GitHub
Practice algorithmic problem-solving on platforms like LeetCode
Build a simple portfolio website to showcase technical projects
internship_strategy.application_stage:
Begin applying once backend and version control
fundamentals are solidly demonstrated; depending on progress, this typically
occurs mid-to-late Year 1 or early Year 2, focusing first on software roles
before pivoting to pure ML.

paths.title:
Applied
Mathematics and Data Science Route
paths.why_it_fits:
Leverages your 'above average' academic
strength in Mathematics and Physics. A degree focused heavily on mathematics and
computing provides the theoretical intuition required to optimize and understand
complex ML algorithms. Comparing B.Sc options can also expand your choices for
finding programs that fit your low-cost preference.
tradeoffs:
Lacks
standard software engineering coursework (like operating systems, networking,
and distributed systems), meaning deployment and production-engineering skills
must be entirely self-taught.

Translating abstract mathematical theory into
deployable, functional code requires high self-discipline and independent
project building.

milestones.focus:
Maintain
basic data handling concepts within the 5-10 hours/week limit

Bridging core math skills with basic
coding and statistics
projects: Personal Expense Analyzer (Processing raw CSV data for trends)

Exploratory Data
Analysis (EDA) on a public Kaggle dataset
End-to-end ML Pipeline (From data cleaning to raw output)

milestones.focus: Bridging the Engineering Gap for ML
projects: Sentiment Analysis Tool served via a RESTful endpoint

Research-based ML project utilizing advanced statistical models with
reproducible environments

internship_strategy.readiness:
Ability
to independently extract data using complex SQL queries, clean messy datasets in
Python, and train standard predictive models with proper validation
techniques.
preparation:
Publish well-documented
Jupyter Notebooks on Kaggle and GitHub

Prepare case studies explaining the
business or research insights derived from your data

Master SQL for robust
data extraction and transformation
internship_strategy.application_stage:
Begin applying once
you can independently perform end-to-end exploratory data analysis and basic
predictive modeling; this capability typically unlocks analytics internship
opportunities by Year 2.
